note: How fast the robot gets hungry, and how full it can get (pluggybot issue
#36). DATA, on the terms rewards.json and cadence.json are: policy about
a world, re-tuned against MEASURED income, changeable on a mounted volume
without a rebuild ($PLUGGY_METABOLISM=/path/to/metabolism.json).
Points are earned by working and consumed by living, and running out when
upkeep falls due is the `unpaid` death (issue #136). The mechanic is the
free time: above `satisfiedAt` the robot's hours are its own.
WHAT 30 AN HOUR IS A FRACTION OF, and it was moved on purpose (#321):
scripted   the rotation on `home`, `--pack hosting`, no overseer: 80
points banked per sim-hour, three chained hours, spread zero
deployed   the LLM pair earns about HALF of that. Over the 7 days to
23 Sep 2026 Rowan was at 0 points in 53 % of the balance
readings and below `hungryAt` in 79 %; Luca at 0 in 18 %.
Once #317 fixed `unminded`, `unpaid` was the first death
(9 of 14 on build e77704c).
So on the served world upkeep was most of the income, and a robot that is
broke half the time acts on hunger: its disposition cannot be read through
it. #321 raised INCOME rather than lowering the rate -- +10 on every job a
board offer pays (rewards.json's note) -- and the rate stays 30. The
scripted figure above is the OLD table's; re-tune the rate only against
the served pair's income read off the observatory under the new one.
⚠ NEVER TUNE ON THE DEMO CELL. There no job was affordable and every point
came from charging (when charging paid), so a rate set there makes charging
the food and work optional. Hosting is the pack the deployment runs.
⚠ THE CYCLE IS LONGER THAN ONE MISSION, and that is the honest reading.
Income is lumpy (a charge, failed jobs, exploring), so work -> satisfied ->
free -> hungry spans several missions, which is why hunger lives in the
ledger and survives a restart. Re-tuning to fit a cycle into one mission
is tuning for a demo.
⚠ ONLY THE SATISFIED LATCH IS HYSTERETIC. The fed/hungry line is a plain
threshold, so an award landing on it followed by a point eaten reads fed
-> hungry seconds apart: measured once a sim-hour, harmless (both states
mean keep working), and not worth a fourth threshold.
THE CAP bounds hoarding and must never be the income. At 90 the robot
spilled 62 of an hour's 80 by its third hour and a heart (200) could not
be bought, so it went to 400 (#136); 600 since #321, room to save for a
heart, since a buy keeps an hour of upkeep back and ~230 must be banked.
Inert until income rises: neither deployed robot came within 100 of 400
in the week to 23 Sep 2026.
`satisfiedAt` and `hungryAt` are a buffer in HOURS OF UPKEEP (45 is an
hour and a half at 30/h), not a fraction of the cap, and do not scale
with it: scaled, the first free time would come hours into a day.
pointsPerHour  points consumed per SIM hour, charged a whole point at a
time (the fraction between carries in the ledger, so a
restart neither wipes hunger nor back-charges it)
cap            the most the balance may hold. Earnings past it are not
banked, and the ledger says how many were refused rather
than dropping them quietly
satisfiedAt    balance at which the robot has had enough and turns to its
own goals
hungryAt       balance at which it goes back to work. LOWER than
satisfiedAt on purpose: the gap is hysteresis, and
(satisfiedAt - hungryAt) / pointsPerHour is how long the
free time lasts
A world block overrides the default block key by key, like cadence.json.
There are none: nobody has measured room_hub's hour, and a per-world
number invented to look thorough is worse than one honest default.
Re-tune whenever rewards.json or cadence.json moves -- both change what an
hour earns -- and measure rather than adjust by feel.
